Resolves #18975

A component could end up with two Responsive plugins. `afterSetResponsive` looked the plugin up before awaiting its import, so two `responsive` values set before the import settled each appended one. Admission is now decided once the import has settled, the pattern #18967 used for `cellEditing`. While fixing that I found a second defect. A component that turned `responsive` off kept its plugin, and the plugin's next resize ran `Object.entries(null)` and threw. `onResize` now idles while `responsive` is off, so one plugin serves every value, `null` included, and the next value resumes it.

Evidence: L1 (unit, real `Neo.plugin.Responsive` instances; the plugin's viewport wiring gets a stand-in, since the unit tier has no main thread to resize) → L1 required (admission and `onResize` are App Worker logic; no DOM is involved). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | `unit/component/ResponsiveAdmission.spec.mjs` › *two values set before the plugin has loaded build one plugin*. RED on `dev` 10/10 with two real instances (`neo-plugin-responsive-1`, `-2`) |
| AC-2 | › *a value set once the plugin exists builds none*. Green on `dev` too, as the control for the behaviour kept |
| AC-3 | › *turned off, the plugin idles through a resize, and the next value resumes it*: `onResize` with a landscape rect does not throw while `responsive` is `null`, and the next value is applied (`cls` contains `wider`) by the same plugin |
| AC-4 | all three arms read `component.plugins` instances, so `getPlugin()` is what they exercise |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The off-state fix is new.** It was measured and then added to the ticket, because the ticket's premise that one plugin serves every later value was false for `null`.
- **Unchanged:** turning `responsive` off still does not remove the plugin. It idles. Removing it would be a separate decision.
